samples.summary: Read-only sheet mount still writes the CRDT root through the cross-sheet recalc path, which the new `readOnly` gate does not cover
samples.evidence: The new constructor comment claims `readOnly` silences "the three writes the grid makes without the user ever running an editing command" (yorkie-store.ts:82-93), but `runRemoteSync(true)` at sheet-view.tsx:1300 runs unconditionally on mount (and again from the remote-change subscription at sheet-view.tsx:1312) for a read-only viewer. It calls `sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas()` → `Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2943-2981), which opens `store.beginBatch()` and runs `calculate(...)`. `calculate` writes cells via `sheet.setCell`/`deleteCell` — unconditionally for spill results (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:118-141) and for cycled cells (line 67) — and `recomputeFilterHiddenRows()` (sheet.ts:2976) writes hidden state. `YorkieStore.endBatch()` then issues a real `doc.update()` (yorkie-store.ts:1176-1187) because `readOnly` is not consulted there or in `set`/`setHiddenState`. So a share-link viewer opening a sheet containing a spilling or cross-sheet formula (or a cycled formula) still performs the `rw` PushPull the PR is trying to eliminate — the viewer's sync wedges exactly as before, and if the webhook were permissive the viewer would be mutating the owner's document.

samples.summary: No-op `ensureAxisOrder` on a read-only mount makes `syncSelectionToPresence` permanently drop the viewer's selection anchors
samples.evidence: `ensureAxisOrder` now returns immediately when `readOnly` (yorkie-store.ts:685-690), but the caller `syncSelectionToPresence` assumes the call may have extended coverage: at sheet.ts:3042 it tests `maxRow > rowOrder.length || maxCol > colOrder.length` and, when true, sets `this.activeCellAnchor = null; this.rangeAnchors = []`. On a read-only mount coverage can never grow, so every selection past the existing `rowOrder`/`colOrder` length (all selections on a sparsely-covered or empty sheet) clears the anchors, and `resolveAnchorsToRefs` then leaves the viewer's visual selection unshifted when a peer inserts/deletes rows or columns — the viewer's selection silently points at the wrong cells relative to the content. Contained (local view state only, no data written), but it is a behavioural regression the new guard introduces in out-of-diff code.

samples.summary: `YorkieDocStore`'s `readOnly` gate is captured at mount but the effect's dep list omits `readOnly`
samples.evidence: The store is constructed with `Boolean(readOnly)` at docs-view.tsx:364 inside an effect whose deps are `[didMount, doc]` (line 581, with `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` disabled). If `readOnly` ever changes without the doc/mount changing (role resolved after first paint, a viewer promoted to editor, a preview toggling), the store keeps the stale gate: a promoted editor never publishes its caret again (peer cursors silently dead), or a mount that started writable keeps publishing presence after becoming a viewer. Current callers (`shared-document.tsx:322/364`, `docs-detail.tsx:280` which passes nothing) look stable, hence low confidence, but the gate's correctness now depends on that being true forever.

samples.summary: Pending DOCX import calls `store.setDocument` on a read-only mount

finding.summary: Read-only sheet mount still writes the CRDT root through the cross-sheet recalc path, which the new `readOnly` gate does not cover
finding.evidence: The new constructor comment claims `readOnly` silences "the three writes the grid makes without the user ever running an editing command" (yorkie-store.ts:82-93), but `runRemoteSync(true)` at sheet-view.tsx:1300 runs unconditionally on mount (and again from the remote-change subscription at sheet-view.tsx:1312) for a read-only viewer. It calls `sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas()` → `Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2943-2981), which opens `store.beginBatch()` and runs `calculate(...)`. `calculate` writes cells via `sheet.setCell`/`deleteCell` — unconditionally for spill results (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:118-141) and for cycled cells (line 67) — and `recomputeFilterHiddenRows()` (sheet.ts:2976) writes hidden state. `YorkieStore.endBatch()` then issues a real `doc.update()` (yorkie-store.ts:1176-1187) because `readOnly` is not consulted there or in `set`/`setHiddenState`. So a share-link viewer opening a sheet containing a spilling or cross-sheet formula (or a cycled formula) still performs the `rw` PushPull the PR is trying to eliminate — the viewer's sync wedges exactly as before, and if the webhook were permissive the viewer would be mutating the owner's document.

verdict.reason: The described code exists as claimed and is reachable. sheet-view.tsx:1300 runs runRemoteSync(true) on mount with no readOnly check (and again from the remote-change subscription at 1306-1313), which calls Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas (sheet.ts:2964-2979). That opens store.beginBatch(), runs calculate(), which writes cells unconditionally on the spill path (calculator.ts:118,136,141), deletes stale ghost cells (calculator.ts:81) and writes cycled cells (calculator.ts:67), all routed through Sheet.setCell/deleteCell (sheet.ts:973-989) into YorkieStore.set/delete (yorkie-store.ts:246-263, 305-322) — neither consults this.readOnly. endBatch (yorkie-store.ts:1176-1208) then performs a real doc.update() whenever the overlay/ops are non-empty. The only readOnly gates in YorkieStore are the presence seed (109), updateSelection (651) and ensureAxisOrder (689); no attach-time or doc-level read-only enforcement was found in the frontend Yorkie layer. So a read-only viewer opening a sheet with a spilling/cross-sheet or cycled formula still mutates the CRDT root, breaking the read-only invariant the change establishes — a real correctness/state-integrity bug on a normally reachable path (major).

searchedFor: packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts (only for query results, not share viewers)
finding.summary: Shared spreadsheet viewer still publishes presence on mount and on every cursor move — under the new enforce-by-default posture this is the rw PushPull that gets 403'd, wedging the viewer's sync
finding.evidence: This change flips the auth webhook to enforcing by default and, on that premise, silences presence publishing on read-only mounts for board (`board-view.tsx:602`), slides (`slides-view.tsx:1137`), PDF (`pdf-collab.tsx:134`) and notes (`readOnlyNoteStore` neuters `setLocalSelection`). The spreadsheet surface was not covered. `SheetView` is mounted read-only for a viewer share link (`shared-document.tsx:283` passes `readOnly`), and `sheet-view.tsx:1012` constructs `new YorkieStore(doc, tabId)` unconditionally; the constructor immediately runs `this.doc.update((_, p) => p.set({ activeTabId: this.tabId }))` (yorkie-store.ts:86-88). `YorkieStore.updateSelection` (line 628) does the same on every cursor move, and it is called unconditionally from the engine (`packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:3045,3058` in `syncSelectionToPresence`, which `setActiveCell` calls). By this PR's own reasoning (`pdf-collab.tsx:124-131`, `slides-view.tsx:1130-1136`) a presence `doc.update()` is a local change the next `PushPull` carries with verb `rw`, which the webhook refuses for a share-link `viewer` — so on any deployment that registers `PushPull` and configures nothing else (now the default), a viewer opening a shared sheet is permission-denied on its first sync. Note also `sheet.ts:3029` calls `store.ensureAxisOrder(...)` from the same presence sync, which can write the document root (rowOrder/colOrder) from a viewer.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts the spreadsheet surface was NOT covered by the read-only presence gate, citing (a) an unconditional presence write in the YorkieStore constructor, (b) an unguarded updateSelection, (c) an unguarded ensureAxisOrder root write, and (d) a two-argument `new YorkieStore(doc, tabId)` at sheet-view.tsx:1012. None of that matches this working tree. The constructor accepts `readOnly = false` (yorkie-store.ts:98-105) and wraps the mount-time `p.set({ activeTabId })` in `if (!this.readOnly)` (yorkie-store.ts:109-113) — the lines the reviewer cited as the unconditional update (86-88) are in fact the explanatory comment. `updateSelection` returns early on `this.readOnly` (yorkie-store.ts:645-651), so the unconditional engine calls from sheet.ts's syncSelectionToPresence hit a no-op; the guard sits at the callee, so caller-side unconditionality cannot bypass it. `ensureAxisOrder` likewise returns early on `this.readOnly` (yorkie-store.ts:685-689), covering the claimed rowOrder/colOrder root write from the same selection path. And sheet-view.tsx:1012 reads `new YorkieStore(doc, tabId, readOnly)`, where `readOnly` is a real component prop (sheet-view.tsx:130,139) and is in the effect dependency list (sheet-view.tsx:1341), so the store is rebuilt if it flips. The only remaining two-argument constructions are test helpers and an archived design doc (tests/helpers/single-user-yorkie.ts:54, tests/helpers/two-user-yorkie.ts:47, tests/helpers/cross-sheet-yorkie.ts:101, tests/helpers/two-user-spreadsheet-yorkie.ts:103-104, tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-axis-order.test.ts:60), which are not product read-only mounts and are out of this lens's lane. The described defect is not present as described.

finding.summary: Shared docs viewer publishes cursor presence through the RAW (unwrapped) store on every cursor move and every remote change — same rw-PushPull denial the PR fixed for board/slides/pdf/notes
finding.evidence: `readOnlyDocStore` is applied only inside the engine (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1075`), so it guards the editor's own writes. `docs-view.tsx` keeps the unwrapped `YorkieDocStore` (line 356) and calls presence mutators on it with no `readOnly` check: `store.updateCursorPos(pos, sel)` at lines 457 and 465 (registered unconditionally at line 452 via `editor.onCursorMove`), and `store.publishResolvedLocalCursor({...})` at line 433, which runs on *every* remote change. Both end in `p.set(...)` inside `doc.update` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1241, 3147). `SharedDocsLayout` mounts `DocsView` with `readOnly` for a viewer share link. With enforcement now the default, the first cursor move (or the first peer edit) makes the viewer's next `PushPull` carry a change → verb `rw` → 403 → the viewer's sync is wedged, which is exactly the failure the PR's own comments cite for the other four surfaces.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts docs-view.tsx keeps an unwrapped YorkieDocStore and calls presence mutators with no readOnly check. In fact docs-view.tsx:364 constructs `new YorkieDocStore(doc, Boolean(readOnly))`, and the store gates both cited presence writes before they reach `doc.update`/`p.set`: `publishResolvedLocalCursor` returns early at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1263 (before the withUpdate/p.set at 1265-1270) and `updateCursorPos` returns early at yorkie-doc-store.ts:3199 (before the withUpdate/p.set at 3201-3206), while keeping only the view-local anchoring at 3191-3194. Both onCursorMove call sites (docs-view.tsx:465, 473), the remote-change publish (docs-view.tsx:441), and the editor-internal setCursorForHistory (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3071) all funnel through those guarded methods; setCompositionStart (docs-view.tsx:450/453 -> yorkie-doc-store.ts:1278-1280) writes no presence. readOnly is derived from the resolved viewer role in SharedDocsLayout (shared-document.tsx:322) and passed at shared-document.tsx:364, stable at mount. So no `rw` PushPull is emitted for a viewer on cursor move or peer edit — the code is not as described.
